title: Japanese university EFL learners’ perceived competence in a guided-autonomy syllabus
text_snippet: Japanese university EFL learners’ perceived competence in a guided-autonomy syllabus Abstract Autonomy-supportive environments are vital in fostering learning motivation, a core feature of the Guided-Autonomy Syllabus (GAS) implemented in Japanese university EFL classrooms. Based on the self-determination theory framework, learning motivation is maintained by satisfying the basic psychological needs of autonomy, competence, and relatedness. Previous research has shown the GAS to satisfy students’ needs for autonomy and relatedness. However, the need for competence remains underexamined. This study explored, within a Japanese university EFL context, (a) the extent to which lectures on how languages are learned, delivered prior to autonomous study in a Guided-Autonomy Syllabus (GAS), were associated with changes in students’ perceived competence in language learning, (b) whether the use of student response systems (clickers) facilitated retention of lecture content, and (c) whether such retention was associated with maintaining perceived competence over the semester. Two groups of first-year Japanese university EFL students participated in the same GAS course that began with these lectures. title: The vocabulary learning strategy use of international students in the academic context in EMI programmes at Hungarian universities: a questionnaire study
text_snippet: The vocabulary learning strategy use of international students in the academic context in EMI programmes at Hungarian universities: a questionnaire study Abstract The acquisition of English vocabulary items related to the academic context, which involve both the so-called academic vocabulary and the field-specific technical vocabulary, is crucial for university students in programmes with English as a medium of instruction (EMI). The use of vocabulary learning strategies (VLSs), especially the types that require active information manipulation, is an individual difference factor in language learning that was found to characterize proficient learners with high vocabulary size. This finding indicates the importance of VLS use in the academic context as well and provides relevance to conduct research about the VLS preferences of international students with diverse backgrounds in EMI programmes at Hungarian universities. title: The co-design of an educational launchpad for improving linguistic proficiency for students in French as a foreign language
text_snippet: The co-design of an educational launchpad for improving linguistic proficiency for students in French as a foreign language Abstract This mixed-methods, design-based study examined the co-design of an educational launchpad for supporting transferable linguistic proficiency among adult university-affiliated learners of French as a Foreign Language (FLE). Grounded in Service Design and operationalised through Action Research cycles, the intervention treated language learning as a service journey in which learners functioned as co-design partners rather than passive recipients of instruction. Fifty-eight Egyptian adult FLE learners ( N = 58; CEFR A2-B1) participated in an eight-week implementation organised around Discovery, Define/Ideate, Develop/Prototype, and Deliver/Evaluate phases. Pretest-posttest outcomes were assessed using a 25-point French proficiency performance test (FLE-PP) and an 8-item Self-Perceived Communication Competence scale (SPCC). Participants showed higher posttest scores on both outcomes, with FLE-PP means increasing from 10.22 to 18.36 and SPCC means increasing from 2.20 to 4.13. Because the study used a one-group pretest-posttest design, these gains are interpreted as changes associated with the launchpad implementation rather than as definitive causal effects. title: Modal verb variations in L1 and L2 written discourse: a corpus-based analysis of can and would
text_snippet: Modal verb variations in L1 and L2 written discourse: a corpus-based analysis of can and would Abstract Modal verbs ( can, could, may, might, will, would ) pose a persistent challenge for both learners and educators despite substantial scholarly exploration of the topic. Using an extensive dataset comprising 2,800 essays, this study investigates the variability in the use of modals among English first language (L1) speakers and second language (L2) learners from Asian backgrounds, focusing on the modals can and would . A comparative analysis of collocational patterns identifies these modals as a major source of divergence between the L1 and L2 groups, notably the prevalent use of the negated form of can and the skewed and restricted use of would among L2 learners. Further, while L1 speakers typically employ would to assert the validity of statements with evidence believed to be indisputable, L2 learners tend to use it when presenting opinions with little or no support. The findings identify specific areas requiring pedagogical interventions for L2 learners, and from a methodological perspective, underscore the importance of complementing corpus-driven results with qualitative analyses when seeking to understand the contextual uses of modals. title: Understanding oral corrective feedback in Chinese university EFL classrooms: a qualitative study of cognitive, affective, and relational processes
text_snippet: Understanding oral corrective feedback in Chinese university EFL classrooms: a qualitative study of cognitive, affective, and relational processes Abstract Oral corrective feedback (OCF) is widely recognised as a key pedagogical mechanism in the development of second language speaking proficiency; however, existing research has largely examined OCF in controlled settings or focused on isolated feedback types, offering limited insight into how feedback is interpreted, negotiated, and enacted within authentic classroom interaction. Addressing this gap, this qualitative study examines how cognitive, social, and affective processes shape teachers’ and students’ experiences of feedback in Chinese university English as a foreign language (EFL) classroom. Rather than treating OCF as a purely technical corrective move, the study conceptualises it as a relational and context-sensitive pedagogical process. Drawing on interactionist and sociocultural perspectives, the study investigates the perspectives of 12 university English teachers and 24 undergraduate students across fluency- and accuracy-oriented speaking tasks. Data were generated through semi-structured interviews, non-participant classroom observations, and stimulated-recall sessions, and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. title: A cultural-context framework of AI-mediated formative assessment: perceptions and proficiency in Iran’s TEFL context
text_snippet: A cultural-context framework of AI-mediated formative assessment: perceptions and proficiency in Iran’s TEFL context Abstract This convergent mixed-methods study introduces a novel cultural-context framework to explore Iranian TEFL learners’ perceptions of AI-mediated formative assessments compared to teacher-led assessments, emphasizing validity, reliability, fairness, and their links to self-regulated learning (SRL) and proficiency gains. Data from 346 learners (B1–C1) across Tehran, Isfahan, and Shiraz were collected over 12 weeks using surveys, interviews, focus groups, and Cambridge tests. Results reveal significant improvements in AI perceptions (e.g., validity: M = 28.4 to 34.6, p M = 36.7 vs. B1: M = 32.8). Both B1 and C1 learners demonstrated significant proficiency gains (writing: B1 +1.5/20, C1 +1.6/20; speaking: B1 +1.0/20, C1 +1.5/20), though between-group differences in gains were small and not formally tested. However, cultural deference sustained teacher-led preference (fairness: M = 42.9 vs. AI: M = 30.8). Institutional trust and technological familiarity drove adoption, while urban-rural disparities (e.g., Shiraz’s connectivity issues) tempered it. title: Exploring ESL pedagogical strategies across diverse learning styles: insights from English language educators
text_snippet: Exploring ESL pedagogical strategies across diverse learning styles: insights from English language educators Abstract Learning styles remain an important consideration in ESL instruction, particularly in engineering education contexts where accommodating diverse learner preferences is crucial for effective technical and professional communication. Despite growing recognition of learner diversity, limited empirical research has examined how ESL teachers in engineering colleges translate this awareness into actual classroom practice. This study employed a convergent parallel mixed-methods design, combining a VARK (Visual Auditory Read/Write and Kinesthetic) based questionnaire administered to 40 ESL instructors with semi-structured interviews conducted with 15 participants across five engineering colleges in the Chengalpattu district, Tamil Nadu, India. Read/Write and Auditory modalities were the most consistently accommodated learning styles across all institutions, reflecting a shared emphasis on traditional lecture-based and text-centered instruction. title: Parent interaction in and attitudes towards Zoom-mediated heritage language maintenance: a mixed methods investigation of Farsi-speaking migrants in Australia
text_snippet: Parent interaction in and attitudes towards Zoom-mediated heritage language maintenance: a mixed methods investigation of Farsi-speaking migrants in Australia Abstract Many minority language speaking migrant families living in Australia are located broadly across the country. Due to this circumstance, computer-mediated language learning, especially that involving video-conferencing platforms like Zoom, represents one way to systematically address concerns around first- and second-generation children’s heritage language attrition. Despite the crucial role of parents in heritage language transmission and the strong potential of videoconferencing in facilitating distance heritage language learning, there is sparse research investigating parents’ involvement in and attitudes towards Zoom-mediated heritage language learning. Mixed methods were used to describe seven Farsi-speaking parents’ involvement in and attitudes towards six Zoom-mediated language learning sessions aimed at supporting their children’s heritage language development. title: Business Chinese vocabulary learning strategies among international undergraduates: usage patterns, group differences, and strategic interrelationships
text_snippet: Business Chinese vocabulary learning strategies among international undergraduates: usage patterns, group differences, and strategic interrelationships Abstract As Business Chinese gains prominence in international language education, understanding how learners acquire its specialized vocabulary becomes increasingly important. This study investigates the vocabulary learning strategies (VLS) employed by 105 international undergraduate students enrolled in Business Chinese courses at four universities in Shanghai. Drawing on Schmitt’s (1997) VLS taxonomy, the research aimed to identify the most and least frequently used strategies, examine differences in strategy use based on learner background variables, and analyse interrelationships among strategy categories. A cross-sectional questionnaire survey was conducted, and data were analysed using descriptive statistics at both category and item levels, t -tests, one-way ANOVA, and Pearson correlations. The findings reveal a moderate overall frequency of VLS use (M = 3.08), with metacognitive, determination, and memory strategies being the most commonly used. At the item level, sustained vocabulary study and contextual guessing were among the most frequently used strategies, whereas flashcards and asking teachers to check self-made vocabulary lists were among the least used. title: Multimodal digital production and the negotiation of identity: a critical pedagogy case study of agency and resistance in EFL writing
text_snippet: Multimodal digital production and the negotiation of identity: a critical pedagogy case study of agency and resistance in EFL writing Abstract The integration of digital technology into English Language Teaching (ELT) has become standard practice. However, research often emphasizes the instrumental benefits of technology for skill acquisition, while neglecting how technology supports critical engagement with the world. This study addresses this gap by exploring the implementation of a critical digital pedagogy in a university academic writing course. Using a qualitative case study design, this research investigates how learners experience this approach and how they use multimodal digital creation to express their identities. title: The use of dialogic pedagogy to enhance STEM students’ argumentation skills and motivation in English language classes
text_snippet: The use of dialogic pedagogy to enhance STEM students’ argumentation skills and motivation in English language classes Abstract One of the goals of educational institutions is to make students problem-solvers. Hence, they design various tasks and initiate extracurricular activities to support learners’ thinking skills. Argumentation skill is one part of thinking and problem-solving skills, which support learners’ creativity, innovation, persuasion, and academic performance. Thus, the purpose of this research was to examine the effects of dialogic pedagogy on STEM students’ argumentation skills and motivation in learning English language courses. The participants were Bahir Dar University Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) students. The study was designed through a quasi-experimental design, in which two groups were selected and assigned to different groups. The data were gathered through oral presentation, key informant interviews, observation, and questionnaire, and the quantitative data were analyzed through independent t-test, One-Way Manova, and Paired sample t-test, and the qualitative data were analyzed through narration. title: Pragmatic competence among non-native learners of Arabic: a cross-sectional mixed-methods study of refusal strategies across proficiency levels
text_snippet: Pragmatic competence among non-native learners of Arabic: a cross-sectional mixed-methods study of refusal strategies across proficiency levels Abstract This study examined how refusal strategy use varied across proficiency levels among non-native learners of Arabic enrolled in an Arabic as a Foreign Language (AFL) program at the University of Ha’il, Saudi Arabia. Using a cross-sectional mixed-methods design, the study analyzed written Discourse Completion Test (DCT) responses from 65 international AFL learners distributed across four proficiency levels. Of the 780 responses initially elicited, 716 valid coded responses were retained after the exclusion of 64 blank, incomplete, illegible, or otherwise non-codable responses. Quantitative analysis classified refusals into three macro-categories—direct, indirect, and adjunct strategies—and summarized their distribution across levels. Results showed a clear proficiency-related pattern: lower proficiency learners relied more heavily on direct refusals, whereas higher proficiency learners used indirect strategies more frequently. title: Task repetition in oral assessment: differential effects in monologue and dialogue
text_snippet: Task repetition in oral assessment: differential effects in monologue and dialogue Abstract Oral assessment is a challenging issue as various factors may play a role in language learners’ production. Task repetition and task type are among factors that may influence oral performance. Previous studies have produced contradictory results about the effect of these two factors. Furthermore, such studies have only focused on one of these factors. Thus, it is yet unclear how these two factors may function in tandem to affect oral performance. The present study was, therefore, aimed at filling this gap. Thirty-two EFL learners carried out four tasks made by combining task repetition and task type: Monologue with exact repetition, dialogue with exact repetition, monologue with procedural repetition, and dialogue with procedural repetition. Four raters evaluated the participants’ speaking performance using the Common European Framework of Reference speaking scale, including descriptors of range, accuracy, fluency, interaction, and coherence. A two-way repeated measures ANOVA was conducted to compare the participants’ performances across the four tasks. title: EFL student teachers’ AI self-efficacy across different countries
text_snippet: EFL student teachers’ AI self-efficacy across different countries Abstract The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) in education has identified the need to understand how future educators perceive and engage with these technologies. This study investigates the AI self-efficacy of English as a Foreign Language (EFL) student teachers across three distinct educational contexts: Japan, Poland, and Slovakia. Recognising the crucial role of self-efficacy in technology adoption, this research aims to compare how pre-service teachers in these countries perceive their capabilities in utilising AI tools for language learning and teaching. The study employed a mixed-method design to collect quantitative data using a specifically designed evaluation scale and qualitative data via an open-ended questionnaire. The sample comprised 98 EFL student teachers from the selected countries. Results revealed observable differences in AI self-efficacy scores among participants from Japan, Poland, and Slovakia, with Japanese participants reporting higher confidence levels than their Polish and Slovak counterparts. title: Academic language challenges in EMI: linking EAP–EMI integration, self-efficacy, and perceived academic success
text_snippet: Academic language challenges in EMI: linking EAP–EMI integration, self-efficacy, and perceived academic success Abstract English-medium instruction (EMI) has expanded rapidly in transnational higher education and has become an important site of second and foreign language learning in disciplinary contexts. Yet how EAP–EMI integration is related to students’ academic language experience and perceived academic success as an institutional learning condition remains underexplored. This study investigates the relationships among perceived EAP–EMI integration, academic language-related challenges, EMI-related self-efficacy, and perceived EMI academic success in a Sino–US transnational higher education programme. Survey data were collected from 405 undergraduate students with sustained EMI exposure and analysed using structural equation modelling. Results indicate that perceived EAP–EMI integration is strongly associated with lower academic language-related challenges and higher perceived EMI academic success. Academic language-related challenges function as an important experience-near mechanism linking institutional alignment to students’ evaluative outcomes. title: The use of electronic chat in French language teaching to develop written interaction skills among faculty of education students
text_snippet: The use of electronic chat in French language teaching to develop written interaction skills among faculty of education students Abstract Written interaction is a core component of foreign language development because it enables learners to negotiate meaning, respond to others, and refine linguistic knowledge in context. This study examined the effect of electronic chat (e-chat) on the development of written interaction skills among students in the Faculty of Education. To this end, the study developed a written interaction skills framework, a student activity booklet, a lecturer’s guide, and a written interaction test. Using a quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test control-group design, the study was conducted with second-year French as a Foreign Language students at Beni-Suef University. After the instructional intervention, quantitative analyses showed a statistically significant difference at the alpha = 0.01 level between the experimental and control groups on the post-test of written interaction in favor of the experimental group, with a large effect size. The experimental group also showed substantial gains from pre-test to post-test. title: GenAI-supported collaborative project-based language learning: effects on EFL undergraduates’ achievement and autonomy
text_snippet: GenAI-supported collaborative project-based language learning: effects on EFL undergraduates’ achievement and autonomy Abstract Despite growing interest in Generative AI (GenAI) in language education, empirical evidence examining its pedagogical integration within project-based language learning and its influence on measurable learning outcomes remains limited. Many studies emphasize learner perceptions or short-term tool interaction rather than sustained classroom interventions grounded in instructional design. Addressing this gap, this explanatory sequential mixed-methods study investigated the extent to which participation in GenAI-supported collaborative PBLL was associated with changes in English language achievement and learner autonomy among EFL undergraduates. Participants were 53 Saudi female first-year university students assigned to experimental and control groups. Data were collected using parallel-form achievement tests, a researcher-developed learner autonomy questionnaire with exploratory construct validation, and thematic analysis of student reflections. Quantitative data were analyzed using linear mixed-effects modelling to examine differential change over time between groups. title: Impact of Artificial intelligence tools on learning motivation in English instruction: a network meta-analysis
text_snippet: Impact of Artificial intelligence tools on learning motivation in English instruction: a network meta-analysis Abstract The rapid expansion of English-Medium Instruction (EMI) programs and the growing demand for English language proficiency have introduced significant motivational challenges for EFL learners who face linguistic barriers. Artificial intelligence (AI) tools offer a potential solution by providing personalized scaffolding and interactive support. This study conducts a network meta-analysis (NMA) of 16 empirical studies (N = 1,923) to compare the effectiveness of three AI interventions, including Generative AI Chatbots, AI Writing Assistants, and AI Language Learning Applications, on the learning motivation of K-12 and university EFL students in English instruction contexts. Results indicate that all AI tools significantly outperform traditional instruction. AI Language Learning Applications (g = 0.907, k = 2) showed the largest effect, followed by Generative AI Chatbots (g = 0.824, k = 11) and AI Writing Assistants (g = 0.692, k = 3). These findings suggest that interactive and adaptive AI tools are particularly effective in fostering motivation by fulfilling students' basic psychological needs of autonomy and competence. title: An exploration of Turkish EFL pre-service Teachers' perceptions on the integration of generative AI in English language Teacher Education: benefits, challenges, and future directions
text_snippet: An exploration of Turkish EFL pre-service Teachers' perceptions on the integration of generative AI in English language Teacher Education: benefits, challenges, and future directions Abstract This study explores the perceptions of pre-service English as a Foreign Language (EFL) teachers in Türkiye regarding the integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into English language teacher education. Employing a quantitative research design, data were collected from 150 pre-service teachers (PSTs) to examine their awareness of AI technologies, perceived impacts on language learning, and acceptance of AI as a pedagogical tool. The findings provide a nuanced understanding of how pre-service teachers engage with AI in educational contexts and emphasise the need for thoughtful pedagogical integration of GenAI tools in teacher education programs. The study highlights the importance of structured, reflective initial teacher education that addresses both the technological affordances and ethical implications of AI use in the classroom. The study also underlines the gender equity in AI adoption, reinforcing that both male and female PSTs share similar levels of engagement with AI technologies. title: The impact of professional development on EFL teachers' literacy practices and self-efficacy
text_snippet: The impact of professional development on EFL teachers' literacy practices and self-efficacy Abstract The present study examined the impact of participation in an annual 60-h national in-service program called Building Blocks (BB), focusing on strengthening teacher knowledge of basic language constructs for teaching literacy in English as a foreign language (EFL). We employed an online questionnaire developed to evaluate teachers’ beliefs and self-reported practices regarding the teaching of reading and writing amongst 50 teachers who had participated in the BB program and 150 teachers who had not. Results using Mann–Whitney nonparametric tests and ordinal regressions indicated that BB participants reported greater confidence in using differentiated instruction methods for teaching literacy to children from diverse backgrounds than non-BB teachers (z = -2.83, p = 0.005). The BB participants also reported greater self-efficacy for teaching reading to students with diverse needs with higher frequency levels than non-BB teachers (z = -3.10, p = 0.002). title: Prompts and recasts in language development: impacts on uptake and grammatical accuracy
text_snippet: Prompts and recasts in language development: impacts on uptake and grammatical accuracy Abstract Corrective feedback is vital for second language development; however, its effectiveness in promoting immediate uptake versus long-term gains remains debated. This study employed a quasi-experimental design to compare the effects of prompts and recasts on the development of conditional sentences and relative clauses among 132 intermediate-level Arab EFL learners at four Jordanian universities. Participants were assigned to four groups, and their performance was measured via a pretest, an immediate posttest and a four-week delayed posttest. Data were analysed using paired and independent samples t-tests to evaluate accuracy gains, alongside Pearson correlation coefficients to examine the relationship between interactional responses and posttest scores. Findings indicated that prompts led to significantly higher rates of immediate uptake (86.1%) than recasts (43.7%). However, both feedback types produced comparable, moderate improvements in accuracy (dz ≈ 0.40–0.44) over the four-week period, with no statistically significant between-group differences. title: When r and β disagree: suppression-aware interpretation of personality-learning links in Vietnamese EFL classes
text_snippet: When r and β disagree: suppression-aware interpretation of personality-learning links in Vietnamese EFL classes Abstract Personality effects in English as a foreign language (EFL) studies are often read from zero-order correlations even though Big Five traits and classroom outcomes are both intercorrelated. Using data from 103 first-year Vietnamese EFL students, this study examines whether such bivariate readings can obscure suppression-compatible patterns. Students completed the BFI-44 and a classroom-adapted inventory of group, individual and kinesthetic preferences, together with a collaboration-oriented self-regulated learning scale. Simultaneous five-trait regressions yielded two notable r → β divergences. Agreeableness was essentially unrelated to individual preference at the zero-order level (r ≈ .02) but became negative after the other four traits were controlled (β ≈ − .15). Neuroticism showed the complementary pattern for group preference, moving from a near-zero bivariate association (r ≈ − .02) to a positive unique coefficient (β ≈ .17). title: Knowledge thresholds of pre‑service efl teachers interpreting traditional Chinese medicine in “journey to the west”
text_snippet: Knowledge thresholds of pre‑service efl teachers interpreting traditional Chinese medicine in “journey to the west” Abstract It is a cultural and pedagogical issue on how to describe Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) by using English. To globalise Chinese cultural heritage, it cannot be realised without TCM. However, the pre-service EFL teachers usually have insufficient knowledge to understand TCM cultural annotation properly from “Journey to the West” . Therefore, this study sets out to identify the knowledge base that pre-service EFL teachers need to acquire in order to comprehend and convey TCM cultural knowledge in the classroom. The theories were behaviourism and andragogy theory of adult learning. A sequential explanatory design was utilised combining surveys and focus group interview. A total of 486 pre-service EFL teachers, 36 teacher educators, 40 medical lectures and 30 medical professors participated in the study. They were recruited by random and purposive sampling technique for different phases. title: The role of comparative continuation tasks in chunk learning
text_snippet: The role of comparative continuation tasks in chunk learning Abstract Chunk learning has been crucial in English-as-a-foreign-language (EFL) learning. This study introduces comparative continuation tasks into chunk learning, exploring whether it can promote chunk learning efficiency. This study adopts an experimental approach which collects quantitative data to assess students’ chunk learning performance. Sixty-two Chinese college students as EFL learners took part in this research. We compared the impact of different chunk learning tasks on acquiring verbal chunks, nominal chunks, discourse chunks and idiomatic chunks in continual phases. The results indicate that (1) comparative continuation tasks yield better chunk learning output than repetitive translation, cloze and recitation; (2) chunk learning develops in an accumulative and dynamic way, and comparative continuation tasks constantly promote chunk learning after several rounds; (3) comparative continuation tasks provide a scaffold for EFL learners to use and imitate. title: A study on the application of ChatGPT in teaching Mandarin near-synonyms
text_snippet: A study on the application of ChatGPT in teaching Mandarin near-synonyms Abstract The current study investigates Chinese as a second language (CSL) instructors’ perceptions and attitudes toward using ChatGPT as a supportive tool for teaching Mandarin near-synonyms. Using few-shot and chain-of-thought prompting, ChatGPT-generated responses were designed to facilitate CSL learners’ acquisition of the near-synonym pairs yizhi/yixiang ‘always/consistently’ and bimian/yifang ‘to avoid/in case of’. Experienced CSL instructors evaluated the quality of the responses using Likert scale ratings across eight criteria, including vocabulary definitions, limitation explanations, situational context, example sentences, error recognition, error correction, overall accuracy, and overall comprehensibility. In addition, instructors rated their level of support for utilizing ChatGPT as an educational tool and provided written explanations for their evaluations. journal_name: Asian-Pacific Journal of Second and Foreign Language Education
title: Effectiveness of GenAI in enhancing writing performance: a meta-analysis
text_snippet: Effectiveness of GenAI in enhancing writing performance: a meta-analysis Abstract This meta-analysis synthesized empirical evidence on the effects of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI)–supported writing instruction on students’ L2/EFL writing outcomes and examined key moderators. Effect sizes were calculated as Hedges’ g and synthesized using random-effects (DerSimonian–Laird) models. Robustness checks included cluster-robust variance estimation (RVE), sensitivity analyses, prediction intervals, and publication-bias diagnostics (Egger, Begg, PET-PEESE). The primary random-effects model yielded a statistically significant pooled effect (g = 0.80, 95% CI [0.37, 1.22]), indicating a large advantage for AI-enhanced writing instruction. Heterogeneity was substantial (I 2 = 92.21%). Publication-bias tests were non-significant. Robust meta-regression showed that risk-of-bias classification significantly moderated effects (β = 0.93, p = 0.014), whereas instructional model, duration, and sample size were non-significant. AI-enhanced writing instruction demonstrates a positive average effect, though effectiveness appears contingent upon methodological and contextual factors.

title: Identities of non-English-dominant teachers-in-training: written discursive representations
text_snippet: Identities of non-English-dominant teachers-in-training: written discursive representations Abstract This study examines how English language teachers-in-training from non-English-speaking countries undertaking language teacher education in an Australian university discursively represented their language teacher identities in their academic writing. Talk-around-text data, comprising excerpts from academic assignments and interviews about these excerpts, were collected from ten teachers-in-training. Six representations of language teacher identity emerged from the analysis: teachers as research-informed practitioners, teachers as facilitators, teachers as language learners, teachers as empowered first language users, teachers as lifelong learners, and contextually responsive teachers. The analysis revealed that the academic assignments provided discursive spaces for the teachers to represent their language teacher identities, which they largely did in disciplinarily-valued and professionally desirable ways. A variety of discursive strategies, such as self-mention, overt mention of identity positions, and use of binary oppositions, were used. title: Academic language-related challenges of EMI students: the case of a private Saudi university
text_snippet: Academic language-related challenges of EMI students: the case of a private Saudi university Abstract This study addresses the academic language-related challenges undergraduate students face in English-medium instruction (EMI) programs and how these challenges vary across individual and contextual factors at a private Saudi university. Given the rapid expansion of EMI in Saudi higher education and the limited context-sensitive, mixed-methods research in this setting, the study responds to an urgent need for empirically grounded evidence to inform pedagogy and policy. Drawing on a mixed-methods design, the study combines survey data from 217 Saudi undergraduates with semi-structured interviews conducted with 16 students. The quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, t-tests, and ANOVA, while the qualitative data were examined through thematic analysis. Instrument validity was established through confirmatory factor analysis, and reliability was confirmed using Cronbach’s alpha coefficients. The findings reveal that students experience moderate levels of language-related challenge overall, with academic writing emerging as the most demanding skill. title: Exploring changes in university students’ persuasive writings with the SFL-based genre instruction
text_snippet: Exploring changes in university students’ persuasive writings with the SFL-based genre instruction Abstract Mastering persuasive writing represents a foundational competency for university students, particularly within academic and professional domains. However, numerous learners encounter enduring difficulties in fulfilling its intricate structural and linguistic demands, thereby necessitating pedagogical interventions supported by empirical evidence. This study aims to explore the changes students make in their persuasive writing practice with each of the three iterations of the Systemic Functional Linguistics (SFL)-based genre instruction. Convenience sampling was adopted with participants consisting of 30 students from an intact class of the English Department in a Chinese university, who were divided into 6 groups. A constructed SFL-based genre teaching model of the four-staged teaching/learning cycle was applied to conduct the instruction. Discourse analysis was used to analyze the group writing compositions. title: The impact of Duolingo usage patterns on motivation and self-perceived speaking proficiency: a quantitative study of Chinese bachelor-level EFL students
text_snippet: The impact of Duolingo usage patterns on motivation and self-perceived speaking proficiency: a quantitative study of Chinese bachelor-level EFL students Abstract With the increasing use of mobile-assisted language learning applications, understanding how different usage patterns relate to learners’ motivation and language outcomes has become an important area of research. This quantitative study examined the relationships among Duolingo usage patterns, intrinsic motivation, and self-perceived oral English proficiency among Chinese undergraduate English as foreign language learners. Guided by Self-Determination Theory, it also explored whether intrinsic motivation mediated the relationship between app use and speaking outcomes. Data were collected from 44 participants using a 25-item questionnaire, and correlation, regression, and mediation analyses were conducted. The results showed that usage frequency was positively associated with both intrinsic motivation and self-perceived oral English proficiency, whereas usage duration was not significantly related to either variable. title: Tailoring AI-powered foreign language learning: a Q method analysis of student preferences for intelligent textbook development
text_snippet: Tailoring AI-powered foreign language learning: a Q method analysis of student preferences for intelligent textbook development Abstract Despite the potential of generative AI to transform foreign language education, existing research on smart textbooks primarily focuses on technical architecture, often overlooking the subjective preferences of learners. This disconnect hinders the development of personalized and effective learning experiences. To address this gap, this study utilized Q methodology to construct a typology of learner viewpoints regarding generative AI intelligent textbooks. Based on the Jobs-to-Be-Done (JTBD) framework, thirty-two foreign language majors (P-set) sorted 48 statements (Q-set) representing various AI functions, content adaptations, and applications. title: Second language anxiety and enjoyment among primary school-aged students: a systematic review
text_snippet: Second language anxiety and enjoyment among primary school-aged students: a systematic review Abstract There is a longstanding consensus that there is a negative relationship between second language (L2) enjoyment and L2 anxiety. However, the extent and nature of this relationship among younger age groups is still unclear. Furthermore, the interchangeable usage of L2 and foreign language (FL) in extant literature presented a significant obstacle for accurate contextual interpretation and generalization of past findings warranting further investigation. Utilizing Bronfenbrenner’s Bioecological Model as an analytical framework, this systematic review investigated the negative relationship between L2 enjoyment and L2 anxiety as well as associated factors to gain a deeper understanding of the negative L2 enjoyment-anxiety relationship among primary school-aged students (6–12 years old). An extensive database search was conducted across five major online databases between 1986 and 2025 supplemented by manual reference searches.
